claims.text: The curve itself is much older than its use in classification. Verhulst introduced the logistic equation in 1838, in a note on the law that population follows in its growth, as a generalisation of exponential growth carrying a maximum value, and estimated its parameters from the populations of several countries. He named the solution the logistic curve in a later paper, and the work was rediscovered only in the 1920s.

source.title: Nicolas Bacaer, Verhulst and the logistic equation (1838), in A Short History of Mathematical Population Dynamics, Springer, 2011, on Verhulst's Notice sur la loi que la population suit dans son accroissement

claims.text: Berkson proposed applying the logistic function to bio-assay in the Journal of the American Statistical Association in 1944, volume 39, pages 357 to 365, and coined the term logit — from logistic unit — advocating it as a simpler and more computationally efficient alternative to the probit model then prevalent. The function describes the log-odds, mapping the open interval from zero to one onto the whole real line so that regression techniques can be applied to probabilities.

source.title: Joseph Berkson, Application of the Logistic Function to Bio-Assay, Journal of the American Statistical Association 39(227):357-365, September 1944, doi 10.2307/2280041

claims.text: Cox set out the regression analysis of binary sequences in the Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B in 1958, volume 20, pages 215 to 232, read before the Research Section on 5 March 1958. A sequence of zeros and ones is observed where the chance that a trial is a one may depend on one or more independent variables, and he considers tests and estimates first for preassigned independent variables and then for variables that are functions of the sequence.

beats.broke: a linear function of the inputs returns any real number, and the thing you want it to return is a probability, which lives only between zero and one
beats.fix: model the log-odds instead: the logit maps that interval onto the whole real line, so a linear model can be fitted there and mapped back through the logistic curve
beats.cost: the coefficients now describe additive changes in log-odds rather than in probability, so the same coefficient corresponds to a large effect in the middle of the range and almost none at the extremes
beats.interview: what goes wrong if you simply fit a straight line to labels that are zeros and ones
